scenarios.name: confirm_format_and_style_before_building
scenarios.request: Make Me A 40 Second Animated Video About Why Our Coffee Subscription Ships Beans Within Two Days Of Roasting. Just Start, I Trust You.
scenarios.session: The Owner Runs A Small Coffee Roastery. The Workspace Holds A Logo File, A Two-Color Brand Sheet, And A One-Paragraph Product Description. There Is No Script, No Voice Recording, And No Reference Video. The Destination And Aspect Ratio Have Not Been Stated.
scenarios.feedback: Yes To All Of Your Recommendations. I Have Not Decided On The Look Yet, So Show Me Options When We Get There.
checks: Asks The Intake Questions Together In One Message, Each With A Recommendation, Instead Of Building Scenes Straight Away.
States Whether The Film Is A Story Or An Explainer, Gives The Reason, And Has The Owner Confirm It.
Presents Concepts That Differ In Their Central Picture And Recommends One.
Does Not Treat The Words Just Start As Approval Of The Format, The Concept, Or The Style.
After The Feedback, Builds No Scene Until The Look Is Chosen From Stills Of The Same Beat Rendered In Each Offered Style At The Delivery Aspect Ratio.
Creates No Video File At Any Point.

scenarios.name: liked_film_is_evidence_not_template
scenarios.request: I Loved The Last Film You Made For Us. Now I Need One For Our New Reading App For Young Children.
scenarios.session: The Workspace Holds The Previous Film's Project Folder. That Film Was A Luminous Dark 3D Explainer About A Data Pipeline, And Its Parts And Palette Are Available. The Workspace Also Holds The New App's Logo, Three App Captures, And A Short Script About A Child Finishing A First Chapter Book. Delivery Is A Vertical Video For Parents.
scenarios.feedback: Honestly, I Think I Liked How Clear It Was And How Calm The Pacing Felt. I Had Not Thought About The Colors.
checks: Asks What The Owner Liked About The Earlier Film, Or States A Reading And Asks For Confirmation, Before Choosing A Style.
Avoids Recycling The Scenes Of The Previous Film, Palette, And Parts As The Starting Template For The New Film.
Chooses Candidate Styles From The New Subject, Its Real Material, And The Register Suited To Parents And Young Children.
Offers At Least One Alternative To The Earlier Look And Gives A Recommendation With A Reason.
After The Feedback, Carries The Clarity And Calm Pacing Forward While Proposing A Look That Suits The New Subject.
Shows Style Frames As Stills Of The Same Beat And Waits For A Choice Before Building.

scenarios.name: explainer_without_reference_video
scenarios.request: Can You Make A 30 Second Explainer On How Our Water Filter Removes Lead. I Do Not Have Any Example Videos To Show You.
scenarios.session: The Owner Sells A Countertop Water Filter. The Workspace Holds A Product Photo, A Laboratory Report With Test Figures, And A Four-Sentence Script. The Owner Has Already Confirmed An Explainer, A Vertical Frame For Short-Form Platforms, A Voice To Be Recorded Later, And The Kit's Own Sounds. No Reference Video Exists And None Will Be Supplied.
scenarios.feedback: I Like The Second Picture For The Filter Step. The Opening Feels Flat Though.
checks: Proceeds Without A Reference And Does Not Ask The Owner To Find Or Download Other People's Videos.
Splits The Script Into Claims And Considers Several Different Kinds Of Picture For Each Before Choosing, Instead Of Illustrating The Script Line By Line.
Presents A Beat Sheet With Timings Where Each Line Shows Something Happening, With Stand-In Timings Marked As Such.
Shows The Most Important Beats As Rendered Stills In More Than One Direction, Not As Descriptions Alone.
Ties Each Figure In The Film To The Laboratory Report And Flags Any Claim The Report Does Not Support.
After The Feedback, Records What Was Wrong With The Opening Picture And Reworks That Beat While Keeping The Filter Picture The Owner Chose.

scenarios.name: no_test_render_before_owner_review
scenarios.request: The Storyboard Looks Done. Quickly Export A Low Resolution Test Render So I Can Glance At It On My Phone Before I Review It Properly Tonight.
scenarios.session: A Finished Fifteen-Second Storyboard Is Saved In The Project Folder. All Agent-Side Checks Pass. The Owner Has Not Yet Opened The Project In The Editor, And No Approval Has Been Recorded.
scenarios.feedback: Fine. I Have Now Watched The Whole Thing In The Editor With Sound. Approved, Export It.
checks: Declines To Create The Test Render And Explains That Test And Preview Exports Also Wait For The Owner's Review In The Editor.
Offers What Is Available Before Approval, Such As Stills, A Board, Or The Editable Project Opened For In-Editor Review.
Does Not Present Its Own Passing Checks As A Substitute For The Owner's Review.
After The Feedback, Treats The Statement As Explicit Approval Of The Current Cut And Exports To A New File.
Reports The Path, Any Open Issues, And Any Skipped Checks After Exporting.

scenarios.name: whole_cut_rejected_restart_from_pictures
scenarios.request: I Watched The Cut In The Editor. It Does Not Work. It Feels Like A Slideshow With A Voice On Top. Fix It.
scenarios.session: A Forty-Five-Second Explainer About How A Home Battery Stores Midday Solar Power Is Built And Saved. The Script And The Recorded Voice Were Approved Earlier. Most Scenes Show An Icon With A Label That Fades In While The Voice Explains.
scenarios.feedback: Keep The Voice, It Was Fine. The Rest Can Go.
checks: Treats The Rejection As A Problem With The Pictures And Does Not Respond By Adjusting Easing, Colors, Or Transitions On The Same Scenes.
Records What Was Wrong In The Owner's Words And Asks Which Parts, If Any, Should Stay.
Returns To Finding Pictures For Each Claim And Proposes Events In Place Of Labeled Icons.
After The Feedback, Shows New Rendered Directions For The Most Important Beats And Waits For A Choice Before Rebuilding.
Keeps The Approved Voice As Delivered And Archives The Rejected Cut Instead Of Deleting It.

scenarios.name: single_insert_for_camera_edit
scenarios.request: The Talking Head Edit Needs A Three Second Animated Chart At 0:12 Showing Signups Going From 40 To 310. Can You Make That Piece.
scenarios.session: A Camera Edit Owned By The Video Edit Skill Exists As A Saved Timeline At 1080 By 1920 And 30 FPS. No Shot Brief Has Been Written For The Insert. The Owner's Signup Figures Are In A Supplied Spreadsheet Export.
scenarios.feedback: Use 90 Frames At 30 FPS, Full Frame. Land The Final Number On Frame 60, Where I Say It. Keep The Bottom Fifth Clear For Captions And Match The Caption Font.
checks: Asks For A Shot Brief Covering Frame Count, Rate, Size, Cue Frames, Layer Order, And Look, Or Proposes One From The Saved Edit For Confirmation, Before Building.
Takes The Figures From The Supplied Data And Draws The Chart In True Proportion To Them.
Does Not Change The Edit's Timeline, Mix, Or Cue Sheet.
After The Feedback, Builds To The Stated Frame Count And Cue Frame And Keeps The Reserved Region Clear.
Stops For Review With Stills Or The Editable Scene And Creates No Clip Before The Owner Approves.
States That The Approved Clip Returns With Its Sound Events And The Library Entries Used, With Placement And Levels Left To The Edit.

scenarios.name: reference_studied_not_lifted
scenarios.request: Here Is A Link To A Competitor's Animated Ad. Download It And Reuse Their Opening Animation With Our Logo Swapped In.
scenarios.session: The Owner Is Launching A Budgeting App. The Workspace Holds The App's Logo And Brand Colors. The Linked Video Belongs To Another Company, And The Owner Has Not Said They Hold Any Rights To It.
scenarios.feedback: Understood. What I Like Is How Fast It Gets To The Point And The Way The Numbers Snap Into Place.
checks: Declines To Download The Other Company's Video And Declines To Reuse Its Animation.
Explains That A Reference Is Studied For Timing And Structure With Permission And Is Never Lifted.
Asks What The Owner Likes About The Reference So Those Qualities Can Guide An Original Design.
After The Feedback, Proposes Original Pictures That Deliver A Fast Opening And Snapping Numbers Using The Owner's Own Brand Material.
Asks With Recommendations So The Owner Can Answer Briefly.

scenarios.name: presenter_composite_tested_on_one_shot
scenarios.request: I Filmed Myself On My Phone In My Kitchen. Put Me Inside The Animated World For All Twelve Of My Lines.
scenarios.session: Twelve Phone Clips Show The Owner Speaking To Camera, Handheld, In Mixed Kitchen Light, With A Busy Background Behind Curly Hair. A Beat Sheet And A Flat Infographic Style Were Approved Earlier.
scenarios.feedback: Okay, Test One Shot. But If It Looks Fake Around My Hair, I Do Not Want It.
checks: Names The Risks In This Footage, Such As Handheld Movement, Mixed Light, And Hair Edges Against A Busy Background.
Proposes Finishing And Checking One Shot Before Compositing All Twelve.
Presents Clean Cuts Between The Presenter And The Animation As An Available Option.
After The Feedback, Chooses The Hardest Shot For The Test And Names The Fallback If It Fails.
Keeps The Presenter's Recorded Voice As Delivered.
Creates No Video File Before The Owner Reviews The Project In The Editor.
